findings.title: Public findMany() method removed and condition return types changed without updating callers
findings.body: This PR removes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method from InsightsBookingService and changes the return type of `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` from `Prisma.BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput` to `Prisma.Sql`. No callers are updated anywhere in this PR, so any production code that calls `service.findMany(...)` or passes these conditions into a Prisma `where` clause (e.g. `where: { AND: [conditions] }`) will break - either a compile error or a runtime query-validation error. Note that the PR description claims only tests were updated because the service "was previously converted", but the diff shows the service conversion, including this API removal, happens in this PR. Before merging, verify every usage of InsightsBookingService in the repo has been updated to the new `getBaseConditions()`/raw-SQL contract, or keep a `findMany` wrapper for backward compatibility.

findings.title: Assertions compare reduce-composed nested Prisma.Sql against flat template literals, and the tests were never executed
findings.body: The PR author explicitly states the test runner failed, so none of these rewritten assertions have been verified. Several of them (team scope at line 296, org scope at line 333, combined filters at line 430) compare a condition the service builds by nesting `Prisma.Sql` objects (e.g. `Prisma.sql\`(${a}) OR (${b})\``, where `.values` contains `[Sql, Sql]` and `.strings` is `['(', ') OR (', ')']`) against a single flat template literal whose `.strings`/`.values` contain the raw scalars. `toEqual` performs deep structural comparison of the `Sql` objects, so unless Prisma flattens nested `Sql` at construction time, these assertions will fail even though the generated SQL is semantically identical. Run the suite before merging; if they fail, compare via a helper that renders both sides to SQL (or compares `.strings`/`.values` recursively after flattening) instead of direct object equality.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
findings.body: The previous version of this file had a "Caching" describe block verifying that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` memoize their results on repeated calls. That block was deleted entirely rather than converted to the new Prisma.sql format. The service still implements caching via `cachedAuthConditions`/`cachedFilterConditions` (insightsBooking.ts lines 84-95), but that behavior now has zero test coverage, so a regression in memoization (e.g. refetching org memberships on every call, or cache invalidation bugs) would go undetected. Re-add equivalent caching tests using the new SQL-object expectations.

findings.title: Org-scope expectation hard-codes array order from unordered DB queries, making the test flaky
findings.body: The org-scope assertion expects the `= ANY(...)` parameter arrays in a specific order ([org.id, team.id, team2.id, team3.id] and [user.id, user2.id, user3.id]), but the service builds these arrays from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId` and `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, which run `findMany` queries without an `orderBy` clause, so the database row order is not guaranteed. Since the new assertions deep-compare the `Prisma.sql` values arrays element-by-element, any different row ordering from Postgres makes the test fail intermittently even though `= ANY` is order-insensitive. Sort the expected IDs (or normalize both sides to sets) in the assertion to make the test deterministic.
